messages:
sre_pager: PROD ALERT: hosted-runtime-3 kv-cache memory spike reaching 95% on gpupool-7, OOM imminent. Affected model: open-compat/7b-v2. Auto-prefetch rates high. Paging to #incidents.
maya (oncall): I'm on it. any customer impact yet?
devon (eng-runtime): Seeing accelerated KV growth for sessions with repeated long prefixes + continuous batching. Top sessions holding ~3.2M KV entries each. That's above our per-session expectations.
luca (eng-infra): Heap graphs: https://grafana/redwood/d/gpu?panel=kv_heap gpupool-7 shows steep climb starting 7092459000.
maya (oncall): timeline? when did it start?
devon (eng-runtime): Starts ~7092457000 after a large customer test ramped synthetic dialogues. Prefetch loop + max_batch_tokens=4096 -> huge KV retention.
opsbot: deploybot: "Started rollout: runtime-config patch kvcap/disable-prefetch for model open-compat/7b-v2 by maya (oncall)" :rotating_light:
maya (oncall): I'm pushing temporary mitigations: 1) disable prefetch for that model 2) apply per-session kv_limit=500000 tokens 3) reduce max_batch_tokens -> 1024 4) set max_batch_items -> 8. Applying now.
devon (eng-runtime): share the quick patch snippet for audit
maya (oncall): ```
# runtime quick patch
models.open-compat/7b-v2.prefetch.enabled = false
models.open-compat/7b-v2.kv_limit = 500000
serving.batch.max_batch_tokens = 1024
serving.batch.max_batch_items = 8
```
devon (eng-runtime): ok making a hotfix patch to the batcher to cap kv mapping growth and avoid prefetch spikes. Will add short-circuit for sessions > 2500 tokens of continuous output.
eng-runtime: patch deployed to gpupool-7 (canary), monitoring.
opsbot: deploybot: "Canary OK -> rollout to gpupool-7 full (5/5)" :white_check_mark:
luca (eng-infra): Memory trending down on gpupool-7, KV heap at 57% now. No OOMs recorded since patch. https://grafana/redwood/d/gpu?panel=kv_heap
customer-success: Heads-up sent to customers who had active long sessions in the last hour. PS: one enterprise customer saw 503s for ~2.5 minutes during the mitigation window and asked for postmortem.
maya (oncall): Customer impact: brief degraded responses, ~0.03% of hosted calls returned 503 for that customer. We routed high-latency traffic to open-compat/7b-v2-quant fallback where possible.
devon (eng-runtime): Root cause hypothesis: prefetch + continuous batching interaction with a long-reuse prefix produced a runaway KV population per session. Batcher combinatorics amplified memory growth.
maya (oncall): Follow-ups: 1) Create INC-2026-483 (postmortem + telemetry) 2) Add per-model prefetch safety caps 3) Add alert for per-session KV > 1M
eng-runtime: created INC-2026-483 in Jira and assigned to devon/luca. Will instrument kv_key churn metrics and make prefetch opt-in for hosted by default.
customer-success: We'll coordinate comms and provide affected customer timeline.
maya (oncall): handing off to devon for long-term remediation. Oncall clear from me. :thumbsup:
devon (eng-runtime): taking handoff. I'll coordinate a canary of a batcher code change that prevents kv growth for repeated-prefix sessions and follow up with a patch timeline.
opsbot: pagerbot: "Incident resolved - mitigation active, monitoring. No ongoing customer-impact. Ticket INC-2026-483 opened."
